memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'Then the priest shall put the woman under oath and say to her, "If no other man has had sexual relations with you and you have not gone astray and become impure while married to your husband, may this bitter water that brings a curse not harm you. But if you have gone astray while married to your husband and you have made yourself impure by having sexual relations with a man other than your husband"—here the priest is to put the woman under this curse—"may the Lord cause you to become a curse among your people." ' - Num 5:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The woman is placed under a solemn oath before God. The whole outcome rests on a truth known only to God and to her own conscience: whether she has been faithful or not. No witnesses, no proof — only what is hidden in the heart, which God alone can see.

This is the deep principle behind this strange old law: God sees what is hidden. Human justice must rely on witnesses and evidence, and sometimes the truth escapes it entirely. But nothing escapes God. He sees the secret act, the hidden motive, the truth no one else knows.

That truth cuts two ways, and both are meant for our good. On one hand, it is a sobering reminder that we cannot hide our sin from God. What we conceal from everyone else lies open before Him (Heb 4:13). This should make us honest and humble.

On the other hand, it is a great comfort for those who are innocent but cannot prove it. When you are falsely accused and no one believes you, God knows the truth. Your vindication does not depend on convincing people; it rests with the God who sees all.

Whichever side you find yourself on today, the same truth applies: God sees the hidden things. Let it drive you to honesty where you have hidden sin, and to peace where you have been wrongly judged.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you live aware that God sees your hidden heart?
- Is there something hidden you need to bring honestly to God?
- How does God's all-seeing knowledge comfort the falsely accused?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see what is hidden in every heart, including mine. Make me honest before You, and comfort me when I am wrongly judged by others. Amen.
